doc.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

chapter: Hearing the bands and the rhythm guitar ideal
title: Hearing every band in New York during the war
summary: He went to see any band, including Spitalny, Spivak, Casa Loma, Ellington, Sherwood and Goodman, to see how they did it.

bands.name: Phil Spitalny and His All-Girl Orchestra

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You know I went to see bands. I listened to everything. Phil Spitalny and his All-Girl Orchestra, Charlie Spivak, Glen Grey and the Casa Loma Orchestra, Duke Ellington, Bobby Sherwood, a wonderful guitar player that nobody knows about that he was a fine guitar player, sort of buried in the studios. But on this occasion he played some very good guitar but basically he was a trumpet player with the band. That was it, he double played all the instruments. Anything. I’d go to see anything just to see how they did it. I didn’t care. Of course, Ellington’s band, because I’d read a little bit and heard a little bit, I’d heard some old records, that was a particular thrill and they were certainly wonderful you know. And Benny Goodman I remember with Mike Bryan on guitar and Slam Stewart. But I would go see anything, just to see how the guys did it. When did they plan, when didn’t they play, why did they do this, why did they do that? You know that kind of thing. Just to see how they all sat, what kind of guitars they were playing, you know.
This was during the war. 1944, ‘45, and ‘46 right after that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
